title: Silent Failure Detection and Mitigation Playbook
author: Aisha Raman
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines detection signals, automated mitigations, escalation flows, and communication templates for "silent" failures — incidents where service behavior degrades without clear error spikes (e.g., high-ratio malformed responses, sudden drop in success-rate, semantic regressions in outputs). Silent failures are high-impact because customers may not receive explicit errors, and traditional alerting can miss them.

Scope: gateway-api, inference-runtime, request-router, kv-cache, and the metrics/observability pipelines that report on them.

Summary of approach:
- Detect: Combine synthetic traffic, user-signal telemetry, anomaly detection (statistical and ML), and health sampling.
- Mitigate: Engage fast failover to cached variants, route to fallback models, or enable degraded mode with explicit customer messaging.
- Restore & Learn: Triage root cause, run postmortem, update detection rules, and schedule a targeted game day.

1) Key signals and detection recipes

1.1 Synthetic checks (primary early-warning)
- Every region runs three synthetic scenarios per minute: short prompt, long prompt, and streaming response test.
- Failure conditions (trigger): response latency > 1.5x baseline OR response token count < 60% of expected OR diffs in structured fields (JSON output mismatch).
- Synthetic check implementation: kubectl exec into synthetic-runner or run via k8s CronJob -> POST to /v1/generate with test prompts and validate schema.

1.2 Customer-facing signal telemetry
- Successful-response-rate (SRR): percent of requests that meet schema and pass quick content checks. Alert if SRR drops by >4 percentage points vs 1h rolling baseline AND absolute SRR < 98%.
- Model-quality edge-case: measured by sample-entropy and hallucination heuristics (semantic-checker). Alert if entropy distribution shifts > 2 standard deviations.

1.3 Infrastructure & proxy indicators
- Unexpected 200-with-empty-body: detect >0.1% of traffic in 5 minutes.
- KV-cache miss spike: cache hit-rate drop >25% in 10 minutes for a customer namespace.
- Router-tail-latency spike without CPU/GPU pressure suggests upstream silent fail.

Prometheus examples (copy-paste)
- SRR anomaly (example):
  sum(rate(inference_response_valid_total[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[5m]))
- 200-empty-body detection (example):
  increase(http_requests_total{status="200",response_length="0"}[5m]) / increase(http_requests_total[5m]) > 0.001

2) Automated mitigations (fast actions)

2.1 Immediate automated responses (0 - 3 minutes)
- If synthetic check fails in >=2 regions OR SRR drop alert fires: automatically enable edge cache-only mode for the affected route for 2 minutes while the alert is routed to on-call. This is implemented by toggling the feature-flag: ffctl set route.<route>.degraded_mode=true.
- Circuit breaker: If router sees 200-empty-body ratio > 0.5% for >1 minute, trip circuit to fallback model (model-fallback:v2) and scale fallback pool by x2. CLI: rctl fallback enable --route <route> --model model-fallback:v2.

2.2 Safe degraded behavior (operator decision)
- Degraded mode behavior summary (recommended): return a 503 with friendly message for non-essential requests; for essential customers, route to cached-response + post-metadata that indicates potential degradation.
- Owner to evaluate: allowlist of customers to receive degraded responses vs. explicit failure.

3) Escalation matrix and on-call responsibilities

3.1 Triage ownership (first 10 minutes)
- Pager: primary SRE oncall (team: eng-sre) receives immediate alert.
- First action (within 5 minutes): acknowledge alert, confirm signal (synthetic logs, SRR graph), and execute automated mitigations if not already in flight.
- If automated mitigation applied, primary documents steps in incident channel and tags owners.

3.2 Next-phase escalation (10 - 60 minutes)
- If issue persists >10 minutes after mitigation: escalate to runtime-owner (serving-runtime) and network-owner (infra).
- Engage product on-call if customer-facing quality implications (samples failing structured output or hallucination).
- Standup a 15-minute bridge if customer-impacting and >30 minutes unresolved. Bridge owner: primary SRE.

3.3 Leadership & customer escalation (>60 minutes)
- Director on-call notified at 60 minutes for any active degradation impacting >2 customers or SRR < 95% company-wide.

4) Communication templates

4.1 Internal Slack (incident channel) — short template:
- [INCIDENT START] silent-failure detected: route=<route> regions=<regions> signal=SRR drop/synthetic fail. Actions: enabled degraded_mode, fallback model routed. Next: triage by @triage_owner.

4.2 Customer-facing status message (Status page snippet)
- Title: Degraded responses for generation API (investigating)
- Body: We are investigating reports of degraded responses from our generation API affecting a subset of requests. Some customers may see shorter-than-expected outputs or missing structured fields. Our team has enabled a temporary degraded mode to reduce incorrect outputs while we investigate. We will provide updates by 30 minutes and again hourly.
- Severity and ETA guidance: If you rely on structured outputs for critical workflows, contact support@redwood.ai with your account id and affected request ids.

4.3 Email template for high-touch customers
- Subject: Incident: temporary degradation of generation outputs (Investigation in progress)
- Body: short summary, mitigation steps taken, expected next update window, support contact, suggested temporary mitigations (e.g., pin to fallback model, increase prompt length).

5) Incident runbook checklist (post-detection to postmortem)
- Immediately: capture event id, affected routes, synthetic-runner output, sample failing payloads, and timestamps.
- Within 1 hour: collect core dumps, gpu metrics, router logs (indexed by trace_id), and sampling of returned outputs (store in secure S3 folder: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/<incident-id>/samples).
- Within 24 hours: assign postmortem owner and file a postmortem draft.
- Within 72 hours: complete corrective actions list (with owners and due dates) and schedule a follow-up game day to validate fixes.

6) Postmortem framing and corrective action examples
- Statement of impact: customers affected, features impacted, SLO deviations (e.g., SRR fell from 99.98% to 94.2% between 02:12–02:44 UTC).
- Root cause hypothesis: model-quantization path selected new kernel that truncates streaming tokens under certain sequence lengths.
- Corrective actions: pin rollout, add unit test for kernel token preservation, update synthetic tests to include failing sequence shapes.
- Verification: create canary group (5% of traffic) with new test harness for two weeks, monitor SRR and entropy metrics.

7) Game day exercises (validation plan)
- Exercise A — Silent-degradation injection: intentionally introduce a semantic checker that mutates a small percentage of outputs without failing responses; confirm detection rules trigger and degraded-mode switches on within 3 minutes. Run quarterly.
- Exercise B — Observability blackout: simulate missing telemetry to verify fallback detection (synthetic checks + sampling).
- Exercise C — Customer escalation simulation: practice high-touch email + status page cadence for 60-minute scenario. Include runbook rehearsal.

8) Ownership and maintenance
- Runbook owner: eng-sre (primary: @oncall-runbook-owner).
- Detection rules maintenance: observability team owns Prometheus/Grafana rules.
- Synthetic scenarios: eng-dx (developer experience) maintains prompt sets.
- Review cadence: review this playbook quarterly and after any silent-failure incident.

Appendices
A) Example logs and traces to collect
- http_access.log sample entry to grep: route=<route> trace_id=<id> status=200 resp_len=0 tokens=0 body_checksum=abc123
- Synthetic-runner output: {"scenario":"long-prompt","latency_ms":342,"valid":false,"diff":"missing_structured_field"}

B) Quick commands
- Toggle degraded mode: ffctl set route.<route>.degraded_mode=true --reason "auto-detected-silent-failure"
- Enable fallback: rctl fallback enable --route <route> --model model-fallback:v2
- Download samples: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/<incident-id>/samples ./samples --recursive

C) Links and references
- Related runbooks: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026
- Synthetic runner code repo: gitlab.internal/redwood/synthetic-runner

End of playbook
